articles.title: Mega-Sena 3073: aposta de Altamira acerta a quina e outras 23 da região levam a quadra; prêmio vai a R$ 230 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos de 9 cidades renderam prêmios a partir de R$ 510,55, com bilhete premiado em R$ 23,1 mil no sudoeste do PA. Ninguém acertou as seis dezenas do concurso.
articles.summary: Jogos de 9 cidades renderam prêmios a partir de R$ 510,55, com bilhete premiado em R$ 23,1 mil no sudoeste do PA. Ninguém acertou as seis dezenas do concurso.
articles.body:
24 apostas registradas no oeste do Pará foram premiadas no concurso 3073 da Mega-Sena, sorteado quinta-feira (22). Um jogo simples de Altamira acertou cinco dezenas (quina), enquanto outras 23 apostas acertaram a quadra. Como não houve acertadores do prêmio principal no país, o valor acumulou.

A aposta que acertou a quina em Altamira garantiu o prêmio de R$ 23.138,67.

Os outros 23 jogos que acertaram a quadra saíram para os municípios de Santarém (9), Itaituba (4), Alenquer (3), Altamira (2), Monte Alegre (2), Almeirim (1), Juruti (1), Oriximiná (1) e Vitória do Xingu (1). O valor pago para a aposta simples com quatro acertos foi de R$ 510,55.

As dezenas sorteadas no concurso foram: 04 — 13 — 23 — 28 — 41 — 58.

O próximo sorteio ocorre neste sábado (24). A estimativa oficial para o prêmio principal acumulado é de R$ 230 milhões.

Mega-Sena bilhete volante Loterias — Foto: Millena Sartori/g1

🗓️ A Mega-Sena tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, às quintas e aos sábados, sempre às 21h.

📶 É possível apostar em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet, no internet banking da Caixa Econômica Federal ou no site ou app das Loterias Caixa, que podem ser acessados por celular ou computador.

O resultado oficial pode ser consultado diretamente nas unidades lotéricas, pelo aplicativo Loterias Caixa ou no site das Loterias Caixa . Para apostas feitas online, o apostador pode conferir a premiação acessando a opção "Minhas Apostas" no app ou site da Caixa.

Os valores líquidos de até R$ 1.700,16 podem ser retirados em qualquer casa lotérica credenciada ou nas agências da Caixa. Valores acima desse limite são pagos exclusivamente nas agências do banco.

Para retirar o prêmio, é obrigatório apresentar documento de identidade original com foto (RG ou CNH), CPF e o comprovante original da aposta impressa. No caso de jogos virtuais, o resgate exige a apresentação do comprovante impresso ou a leitura do QR Code gerado pelo app ou site das Loterias Caixa. Prêmios online dentro do limite de isenção também podem ser transferidos para uma conta Mercado Pago.

O ganhador tem até 90 dias corridos, contados a partir da data do sorteio, para resgatar o valor. Após esse prazo, o prêmio prescreve e os recursos são repassados ao Tesouro Nacional para aplicação no Fundo de Financiamento Estudantil (FIES).

O valor divulgado pela Caixa Econômica Federal é líquido, pois a alíquota de 30% do Imposto de Renda já é retida diretamente na fonte. O montante informado na tabela de premiação é pago integralmente ao apostador no momento do resgate.

Quando nenhum apostador acerta as seis dezenas sorteadas em concursos regulares, o prêmio principal fica acumulado para a faixa de seis acertos do concurso seguinte.

articles.title: Júri de acusados por matar e esquartejar jogador é adiado | G1
articles.standfirst: Julgamento estava marcado para 26 de outubro, em Amambai, mas foi adiado após o advogado de um dos réus sofrer uma fratura no pé. O crime ocorreu em junho de 2023, em Sete Quedas.
articles.summary: Julgamento estava marcado para 26 de outubro, em Amambai, mas foi adiado após o advogado de um dos réus sofrer uma fratura no pé. O crime ocorreu em junho de 2023, em Sete Quedas.
articles.body:
O julgamento dos cinco acusados pela morte do jogador de futebol Hugo Vinicius Skulny Pedrosa, de 19 anos, foi adiado para 22 de fevereiro de 2027, às 8h, em Amambai (MS). A sessão estava marcada para a próxima segunda-feira (26), mas foi cancelada após o advogado de um dos réus sofrer uma fratura no pé esquerdo.

Hugo foi morto a tiros em junho de 2023, em Sete Quedas (MS). Segundo a denúncia do Ministério Público, o corpo do jovem foi esquartejado e partes dos restos mortais foram jogadas no rio Iguatemi.

A decisão que adiou o júri foi assinada na quinta-feira (22) pelo juiz Renan da Silva Pinto, da Vara Criminal da Comarca de Amambai. O magistrado aceitou o pedido da defesa de Danilo Alves Vieira da Silva, cujo advogado, Higo dos Santos Ferré, apresentou atestado médico com recomendação de afastamento do trabalho por 45 dias.

Conforme os documentos apresentados à Justiça, o advogado fraturou um dos ossos do pé esquerdo. Ele recebeu recomendação para manter o membro imobilizado e evitar apoiar o pé no chão ou permanecer em pé por períodos prolongados.

Na decisão, o juiz considerou que o problema de saúde impede a participação do advogado no julgamento e que o adiamento é necessário para garantir o direito de defesa do acusado.

A Justiça também levou em conta a falta de datas disponíveis para julgamentos até o fim de 2026. O magistrado rejeitou a possibilidade de dividir o processo, o que levaria à realização de dois júris sobre os mesmos fatos.

Assassinato de jogador: montagem com fotos de Hugo Vinicius Skulny Pedrosa, Danilo Alves Vieira e Rubia Joice de Oliver Luvisetto — Foto: g1

Três dos acusados respondem por homicídio qualificado e ocultação de cadáver: Rúbia Joice de Oliver Luvisetto, ex-namorada de Hugo na época do crime; Danilo Alves Vieira da Silva; e Cleiton Torres Vobeto.

Os pais de Rúbia, Patrick Eduardo do Nascimento e Noemi Matos de Oliver, também serão julgados, mas respondem por fraude processual. Segundo a acusação, eles teriam ajudado a ocultar provas do crime.

A previsão inicial era de que o julgamento durasse até dois dias, devido à complexidade do caso. A Justiça determinou que os envolvidos sejam comunicados sobre a nova data.

Hugo foi morto em 25 de junho de 2023, depois de sair de uma festa em Pindoty Porã, no Paraguai. Segundo a denúncia do Ministério Público, ele foi deixado por amigos nas proximidades da casa da ex-namorada, em Sete Quedas.

Ainda conforme a acusação, Rúbia teria atraído o jovem até uma residência, onde ela e Danilo teriam cometido o assassinato. Depois, o corpo foi esquartejado e partes dos restos mortais foram jogadas no rio Iguatemi, com a participação de Cleiton, segundo a denúncia.

O desaparecimento foi registrado pela mãe do jovem, Eliana Skulny, em 26 de junho daquele ano. Durante sete dias, moradores e equipes de segurança participaram das buscas.

Partes do corpo foram encontradas no rio Iguatemi em 2 de julho de 2023, durante uma força-tarefa que reuniu as polícias Civil e Militar, o Corpo de Bombeiros e a Delegacia Especializada de Repressão aos Crimes de Fronteira (Defron).

O reconhecimento foi feito por meio de uma tatuagem no braço do jovem com o nome do pai, que havia morrido cerca de dois anos antes.

articles.title: Enfermeira do DF que morreu em Portugal teve alergia | G1
articles.standfirst: Amanda Marinho Nascimento estava com o marido em viagem de lua de mel. Conselho Regional de Enfermagem publicou nota de pesar.
articles.summary: Amanda Marinho Nascimento estava com o marido em viagem de lua de mel. Conselho Regional de Enfermagem publicou nota de pesar.
articles.body:
Amanda Marinho Nascimento, enfermeira do DF, e o marido — Foto: Reprodução

A enfermeira Amanda Marinho Nascimento , moradora do Distrito Federal, morreu na quarta-feira (21) durante a viagem de lua de mel para Portugal . De acordo com familiares, Amanda, de 29 anos, passou mal após comer frutos do mar durante o almoço, em um restaurante em Portugal.

Amanda atuava na UTI de um hospital particular em Taguatinga, no DF. O g1 tenta contato com a família.

A reação alérgica aconteceu duas horas depois da refeição, enquanto Amanda e o marido visitavam pontos turísticos de Leiria, a cerca de 120 km de Lisboa , capital do país.

Segundo o cunhado de Amanda, ela era alérgica a frutos do mar . Ao perguntar aos funcionários do restaurante sobre os ingredientes do prato, teria entendido que o alimento servido era peixe. Ela sofreu uma parada cardíaca e morreu ainda a caminho do hospital.

De acordo com amigos, o valor necessário para trazer o corpo de Amanda para o DF já foi arrecadado, por meio de uma vaquinha.

Enfermeira do DF morre durante lua de mel em Portugal/Coren-DF divulgou nota de pesar — Foto: Reprodução

O Conselho Regional de Enfermagem do DF (Coren-DF) e o hospital Mantevida, onde Amanda trabalhava, publicaram notas de pesar.

"Neste momento de tristeza, nos solidarizamos com seus familiares, amigos e colegas de trabalho, desejando força e serenidade para enfrentar a dor da despedida. O Conselho manifesta suas condolências a todos os que foram impactados por sua partida e se solidariza com seus familiares e colegas neste momento de luto", diz o conselho.

O grupo de orações do qual Amanda participava com o marido, Tiago, também publicou mensagens de pesar. Segundo o perfil, a família ainda tenta juntar os recursos financeiros necessários para a repatriação do corpo.

Em nota, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores informou que permanece à disposição para prestar assistência por meio do Consulado-Geral do Brasil no Porto.

"O atendimento consular prestado pelo estado brasileiro é feito a partir de contato do cidadão interessado ou, a depender do caso, de sua família. A atuação consular do Brasil pauta-se pela legislação internacional e nacional", diz o ministério.

articles.title: Apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro fazem caminhada em Juiz de Fora | G1
articles.standfirst: Ato aconteceu na noite desta quinta-feira (22), com concentração em frente ao prédio da Câmara Municipal.
articles.summary: Ato aconteceu na noite desta quinta-feira (22), com concentração em frente ao prédio da Câmara Municipal.
articles.body:
Apoiadores do candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) realizaram uma passeata pelo Centro de Juiz de Fora . O ato aconteceu na noite desta quinta-feira (22), com concentração em frente ao prédio da Câmara Municipal.

A manifestação começou por volta das 18h, e os participantes caminharam pelo Calçadão da Rua Halfeld e seguiram até a esquina com a Rua Batista de Oliveira.

A mobilização também reuniu figuras públicas da cidade, incluindo deputados, vereadores e representantes do PL.

Com cartazes, bandeiras e um caminhão de som, o grupo manifestou apoio ao candidato. O ato foi pacífico e não houve registro de ocorrências.

Apoiadores do candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) realizaram uma passeata pelo Centro de Juiz de Fora — Foto: Elton Moreira/TV Integração

O segundo turno para escolha do novo presidente será no próximo domingo (25). Ao todo, 395.457 eleitores estão aptos a votar em Juiz de Fora.

No primeiro turno, Lula foi o candidato a presidente mais votado no município, com 151.552 votos. Já Flávio Bolsonaro recebeu 126.964 votos.

articles.title: Bazar em Curitiba tem roupas infantis a partir de R$ 2 no sábado (24) | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento será realizado das 8h às 13h e terá brincadeiras e lanche para as crianças.
articles.summary: Evento será realizado das 8h às 13h e terá brincadeiras e lanche para as crianças.
articles.body:
Bazar em Curitiba tem roupas infantis e brinquedos a partir de R$ 2 neste sábado (24) — Foto: Reprodução

Um bazar beneficente terá roupas infantis e brinquedos com preços a partir de R$ 2 neste sábado (24), em Curitiba .

A ação é promovida pela Socorro aos Necessitados, entidade responsável pelo Lar dos Idosos Recanto do Tarumã, e será realizado das 8h às 13h, na Rua Konrad Adenauer, 576, Tarumã.

Além dos produtos infantis, o público poderá comprar roupas femininas e masculinas, móveis usados e itens remanescentes de um bazar anterior, que reuniu mercadorias apreendidas pela Receita Federal.

A programação também inclui brincadeiras e lanche para as crianças, como pipoca, doces, bolos e gelatina.

Arrecadação ajuda a manter lar de idosos

A renda obtida com o bazar será destinada à manutenção do Lar dos Idosos Recanto do Tarumã, que acolhe atualmente 119 homens idosos em situação de vulnerabilidade social.

Os idosos são encaminhados à instituição pela Fundação de Ação Social (FAS) e pela Secretaria de Estado do Desenvolvimento Social e Família (SEDEF).

Além de comprar os produtos, a população pode doar itens para serem comercializados permanentemente pela instituição.

Fundada em 1921, a entidade completou 105 anos de atuação em setembro. A instituição filantrópica atende pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade social e conta com profissionais de diferentes áreas, como medicina, enfermagem, fisioterapia, psicologia, terapia ocupacional e assistência social.

articles.title: Embraer: carteira de pedidos bate recorde de US$ 35,7 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Fabricante de São José dos Campos registrou novo recorde histórico, com alta de 14% em um ano.
articles.summary: A Embraer alcançou US$ 35,7 bilhões em pedidos no terceiro trimestre, impulsionada pela aviação comercial e novos contratos de defesa e jatos executivos.
articles.body:
Vista da sede da Embraer, em São José dos Campos, interior de SP — Foto: Luis Lima Jr./Futura Press/Estadão Conteúdo

A Embraer, fabricante de aeronaves com sede em São José dos Campos (SP), bateu recorde na carteira de pedidos pelo sétimo trimestre consecutivo. O valor chegou a US$ 35,7 bilhões entre julho e setembro deste ano, alta de 14% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. O balanço com os resultados do terceiro trimestre foi divulgado pela empresa nesta sexta-feira (23).

Segundo a empresa, o valor do trimestre também supera em 3% o recorde anterior, registrado no segundo trimestre deste ano, entre abril e junho.

A aviação comercial concentrou a maior parte dos pedidos, com US$ 15,8 bilhões. Entre os negócios fechados no trimestre estão encomendas de jatos da família E2 por companhias aéreas internacionais.

O Grupo Abra fez um pedido firme de 20 aeronaves E195-E2, além de opções e direitos de compra que podem elevar a encomenda a até 45 aviões. A Binter encomendou outras cinco unidades do mesmo modelo, enquanto a japonesa ANA Holdings pediu mais oito E190-E2.

No acumulado do ano, a Embraer recebeu 72 pedidos firmes para aeronaves da família E2.

A carteira de pedidos da aviação executiva chegou a US$ 8,2 bilhões, alta de 12% na comparação com o terceiro trimestre de 2025. O resultado também representa um recorde para o segmento, que inclui jatos particulares das famílias Phenom e Praetor.

Durante o trimestre, a Embraer lançou o Phenom 300EV, uma evolução do jato leve Phenom 300. O modelo recebeu certificações de autoridades aeronáuticas do Brasil, dos Estados Unidos e da Europa.

A divisão de Defesa e Segurança encerrou o trimestre com US$ 6,1 bilhões em pedidos, crescimento de 56% em um ano. Um dos destaques foi o contrato para a venda de dois aviões militares KC-390 Millennium à Força Aeroespacial Colombiana.

Já a carteira de Serviços e Suporte chegou a US$ 5,6 bilhões, alta de 14% na comparação anual. O segmento reúne contratos de manutenção, suporte técnico e outros serviços para aeronaves comerciais, executivas e militares.

articles.title: São Miguel Arcanjo: chuvas causam transtornos no Brejaúva há 10 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Famílias que vivem no bairro Brejaúva ficam ilhadas e sem ter acesso a serviços essenciais. Prefeitura afirma que fez uma vistoria no local e fará um reparo emergencial para evitar os transtornos.
articles.summary: Moradores do bairro Brejaúva, em São Miguel Arcanjo, enfrentam problemas causados por fortes chuvas há mais de 10 anos.
articles.body:
Os moradores do bairro Brejaúva, em São Miguel Arcanjo (SP), enfrentam transtornos sempre que fortes chuvas atingem a cidade. Segundo a população, os problemas se arrastam há mais de dez anos.

Ao todo, 18 famílias vivem no local e a maioria vive da agricultura, incluindo o morador Luiz Antônio Flauzino. A água é essencial para a rotina do ramo, mas, segundo ele, o abascimento tem sido motivo de preocupação.

O agricultor fez uma boca de lobo improvisada para tentar escoar a água, mas a alternativa não foi suficiente. A água entra na casa e invade as estufas onde ele cultiva as plantações, fazendo com que ele deixasse de plantar em certos pontos da propriedade.

"Entra água, lama, cascalho. Já enchemos uma fossa e a água dela entrou dentro de casa. Arrumamos, demos um jeito, mas os tubos estão todos fechados. Quando chove forte, vem tudo de novo", lamenta Luiz.

Moradores enfrentam dificuldades há mais de dez anos — Foto: Ricardo Kern/TV TEM

Durante e depois de tempestades, as famílias ficam ilhadas no bairro, e crianças e adolescentes enfrentam dificuldades para chegar à escola. Segundo a moradora Josiele Nogueira, as estradas ficam cobertas de lama e intransitáveis, impedindo a passagem do transporte escolar.

"A van fala de chegar até um certo ponto do bairro e tentamos passar, mas não dá. Nem a pé. Certo dia, tentei passar com as crianças e eu caí no meio do bairro. Precisamos voltar, porque não tem como ir à escola sujo de barro. Eles ficam sem frequentar aulas", desabafa.

Moradores de bairro rural em São Miguel Arcanjo enfrentam dificuldades de deslocamento sempre que chove — Foto: Ricardo Kern/TV TEM

O morador Luiz Amaral afirma que a situação piorou após a prefeitura colocar cascalho na via. Segundo ele, a rua ficou mais alta do que as casas, fazendo com que a água da chuva escorra diretamente da estrada para dentro dos imóveis.

"Aqui, precisa ser feito um projeto com tubulação e a prefeitura não parece estar interessada. Falta um pouco de engenharia da prefeitura, para fazer um trabalho mais adequado e que eles não percam dinheiro, tempo e trabalho. Tudo isso resolveria o problema, que dá sim para resolver", comenta.

Luiz Antônio é morador do local e sofre com transtornos causados pela chuva — Foto: Ricardo Kern/TV TEM

Em nota enviada à TV TEM , a Prefeitura de São Miguel Arcanjo informou que fez uma vistoria no bairro Brejaúva e que um serviço emergencial será realizado a fim de evitar que a água da chuva continue descendo em direção às casas.

A administração municipal ainda afirma que, após o período de chuvas, pretende instalar tubulações e fazer manobras para, assim, desviar a água das residências.

Além da lama, moradores relatam que a água repressada invade as casas — Foto: Ricardo Kern/TV TEM

articles.title: Funcionários da Volkswagen ameaçam greve na Alemanha | G1
articles.standfirst: Sindicato dá prazo até o fim de outubro para montadora recuar do cancelamento de negociações. Conselho aponta plano para congelar remunerações até 2030.
articles.summary: Sindicato dá prazo até o fim de outubro para montadora recuar do cancelamento de negociações. Conselho aponta plano para congelar remunerações até 2030
articles.body:
Volkswagen Tiguan na linha de produção de Wolfsburg, Alemanha. — Foto: Divulgação / VW

Os funcionários da Volkswagen na Alemanha ameaçaram entrar em greve a partir de janeiro se a montadora não reverter o cancelamento de acordos salariais . O sindicato IG Metall estabeleceu o final de outubro como prazo para que a empresa recue da decisão. As informações são da Reuters

A mobilização ocorre após a Volkswagen encerrar contratos que garantiam padrões trabalhistas históricos na companhia. A medida imposta pela gestão afetou negociações sobre o pagamento de férias e regras de jornada de trabalho.

Em meio ao impasse, o conselho de trabalhadores informou que a diretoria executiva planeja congelar os salários de 660 mil funcionários em todo o mundo até o ano de 2030 . O corte de custos tenta conter os impactos da concorrência chinesa, das despesas com tarifas e dos gastos com a transição para veículos elétricos.

O plano de reestruturação da montadora europeia pode atingir 100 mil postos de trabalho . A empresa também avalia o fechamento de até quatro fábricas no território alemão.

Segundo a Reuters, o negociador principal do sindicato IG Metall, Thorsten Groeger, afirmou que uma ação massiva será iniciada caso a empresa não retire o aviso de rescisão dos acordos.

Ele declarou que as mobilizações vão preparar o caminho para greves , que atualmente estão proibidas por uma trégua em vigor até o primeiro dia de janeiro.

A chefe do conselho de trabalhadores, Daniela Cavallo, destacou que as mudanças nas condições operacionais do mercado eram previsíveis. Ela pontuou que os funcionários esperam que a diretoria atue em conjunto com as lideranças trabalhistas para encontrar uma solução .

Fábrica da Volkswagen em Wolfsburg, Alemanha. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A Volkswagen, diz a Reuters, não comentou as medidas específicas de redução de gastos . As negociações salariais oficiais estão previstas para começar, no máximo, no início de dezembro, mas o sindicato pede que as conversas sejam antecipadas para o dia 24 de novembro.

Uma das alternativas em análise é a criação de uma estrutura de transição . O formato contaria com o apoio da agência federal de emprego alemã para requalificar profissionais e auxiliar na busca por novas vagas fora da montadora.

articles.title: Pedreiro morre após ser atingido por disparo de arma caseira que encontrou em obra em Imperatriz, no MA  | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 40 anos teria manuseado a arma e atingido a própria coxa acidentalmente. Polícia investiga as circunstâncias da morte.
articles.summary: Vítima de 40 anos teria manuseado a arma e atingido a própria coxa acidentalmente. Polícia investiga as circunstâncias da morte.
articles.body:
Um pedreiro de 40 anos morreu após ser atingido por um disparo de uma arma de fabricação caseira, conhecida como bodoque, na manhã de quinta-feira (22), no bairro Vale do Sol, em Imperatriz , no Maranhão.

A vítima foi identificada como Mazoleni Silva Pajaú. Segundo informações da polícia, ele trabalhava em uma construção quando encontrou a arma, geralmente utilizada em atividades de caça e capaz de lançar pequenos projéteis.

Ainda de acordo com a polícia, a suspeita é de que o trabalhador tenha manuseado o objeto sem saber do que se tratava e acabou atingindo a própria coxa acidentalmente. O disparo provocou uma hemorragia.

Mazoleni foi socorrido por pessoas que estavam no local e levado às pressas para o Hospital Municipal de Imperatriz. Apesar do atendimento, ele não resistiu à gravidade do ferimento e morreu na unidade de saúde.

Pedreiro morre após ser atingido por disparo de arma caseira que encontrou em obra em Imperatriz, no MA — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

A polícia investiga as circunstâncias da morte para esclarecer se o disparo foi realmente acidental. Os investigadores também buscam identificar o proprietário da arma e descobrir como ela foi parar na construção.

A orientação da polícia é que, ao encontrar uma arma de fabricação caseira ou qualquer objeto semelhante, a população evite manuseá-lo e acione as autoridades.

articles.title: Denúncias de assédio eleitoral sobem 136% em MS; veja como denunciar | G1
articles.standfirst: MPT recebeu 29 denúncias até 22 de outubro, contra 11 registradas até o primeiro turno; órgão fará plantão durante o fim de semana da votação
articles.summary: MPT recebeu 29 denúncias até 22 de outubro, contra 11 registradas até o primeiro turno; órgão fará plantão durante o fim de semana da votação
articles.body:
O número de denúncias de assédio eleitoral em Mato Grosso do Sul aumentou 136,4% após o primeiro turno das eleições de 2026. Até quinta-feira (22), o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT-MS) recebeu 29 denúncias no estado. Antes da votação de 4 de outubro, eram 11 registros.

Com o aumento dos relatos na reta final da disputa eleitoral, o órgão manterá um plantão durante o fim de semana da eleição para receber denúncias de trabalhadores que sofreram pressão, ameaças ou constrangimentos relacionados à preferência política ou ao voto.

O canal de denúncias ficará disponível 24 horas por dia, inclusive durante o fim de semana da votação.

Segundo a procuradora-chefe do MPT-MS, Cândice Arosio, o aumento dos registros pode estar relacionado à maior conscientização dos trabalhadores sobre o que caracteriza o assédio eleitoral e como denunciar esse tipo de situação.

A procuradora reforça que nenhum trabalhador pode ser pressionado ou ameaçado por causa de suas escolhas políticas.

“O aumento das denúncias pode estar relacionado à maior conscientização dos eleitores sobre o que caracteriza o assédio eleitoral e como denunciá-lo. É importante que os trabalhadores saibam que a liberdade de escolha política deve ser respeitada e que práticas de coação ou constrangimento no ambiente de trabalho podem ser denunciadas ao Ministério Público do Trabalho”, afirmou.

Ministério Público do Trabalho de Mato Grosso do Sul — Foto: Google Street View

As denúncias podem ser feitas pela internet, por meio do canal oficial do Ministério Público do Trabalho em Mato Grosso do Sul , que funciona 24 horas por dia.

O assédio eleitoral acontece quando alguém usa a relação de trabalho para tentar influenciar ou controlar a escolha política de um funcionário. Isso pode ocorrer por meio de ameaças, intimidações, constrangimentos ou outras formas de pressão relacionadas ao voto.

As situações também podem envolver manifestações em ambientes digitais, dependendo das circunstâncias e dos possíveis efeitos sobre a liberdade de escolha do trabalhador.

O MPT orienta que os casos sejam denunciados para que possam ser apurados. O recebimento de relatos não termina no dia da votação: o órgão continua analisando as denúncias após o encerramento das eleições e pode adotar medidas quando irregularidades forem constatadas.

Os dados do MPT-MS mostram que os registros aumentaram ao longo dos meses e se concentraram em outubro, período de votação.

Até o primeiro turno, realizado em 4 de outubro, o estado tinha 11 registros. Desde então, foram contabilizadas mais 18 denúncias, elevando o total para 29.

Em comparação com as eleições presidenciais de 2022, quando Mato Grosso do Sul registrou 58 denúncias de assédio eleitoral, o número atual equivale à metade do total daquele pleito.

Em todo o país, o Ministério Público do Trabalho recebeu 674 denúncias de assédio eleitoral em outubro de 2026, até o dia 20. Em setembro, foram 552 registros.

De janeiro a outubro deste ano, o total nacional chegou a 1.492 denúncias.

Nas eleições presidenciais de 2022, o MPT recebeu 3.373 denúncias em todo o Brasil. Desse total, 2.641 foram registradas em outubro, mês da votação.

Os números mostram que os relatos de assédio eleitoral tendem a se concentrar na fase decisiva do calendário eleitoral, quando aumenta a pressão sobre os trabalhadores em razão de suas escolhas políticas.

articles.title: França vai mobilizar 70 mil agentes de segurança para conter protestos | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, apelos à violência e a saques já circulam nas redes sociais. Na última quinta-feira (22), milhares de pessoas voltar às ruas de Paris.
articles.summary: Segundo o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, apelos à violência e a saques já circulam nas redes sociais. Na última quinta-feira (22), milhares de pessoas voltar às ruas de Paris
articles.body:
A França vai mobilizar cerca de 70 mil agentes de segurança em todo o país para as novas manifestações previstas para este fim de semana, afirmou o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, nesta sexta-feira (23).

Ele alertou que apelos à violência e a saques já circulam nas redes sociais.

"Identificamos numerosos apelos de movimentos de extrema esquerda e de extrema esquerda radical", disse Nunez em uma coletiva de imprensa.

Segundo o ministro, o efetivo mobilizado vai incluir unidades policiais de elite, cerca de 20 veículos blindados e 15 veículos com canhões de água.

Na última quinta-feira (22), milhares de pessoas foram às ruas de Paris, enquanto outras cidades francesas proibiram manifestações após confrontos e saques registrados no fim de semana . Os episódios foram considerados os mais violentos dos últimos anos no país.

Desde o último sábado (17), 2.700 pessoas foram presas em razão das manifestações e das invasões de estabelecimentos comerciais, segundo o ministro da Justiça francês, Gerald Darmanin.

Novas proibições são esperadas para os próximos dias. O presidente da França, Emmanuel Macron , afirmou que as medidas têm como objetivo proteger os centros das cidades, os estabelecimentos comerciais e os prédios públicos.

O direito à manifestação é protegido pela Constituição francesa. Grupos de estudantes do ensino médio e universitários afirmaram que continuarão mobilizados, apesar do início do recesso escolar de outono nesta semana.

Macron atribuiu a violência do fim de semana a ações de grupos de extrema esquerda radical que, segundo ele, pretendiam derrubar a República , além de criminosos interessados em saquear estabelecimentos .

A onda de distúrbios em Paris e em outras cidades levou as autoridades a reforçar a segurança. Toques de recolher noturnos foram adotados em algumas regiões da capital e em outros municípios onde a situação já havia sido controlada .

Pessoas observam e tiram fotos dos trabalhos de limpeza em Paris após protestos contra o custo de vida, no fim de semana, terminarem em tumultos e saques em várias partes da França. — Foto: Teresa Suarez / AP

França prepara operação de segurança para novos protestos

As manifestações da quinta-feira foram consideradas uma preparação para um grande ato previsto para sábado (24). A expectativa é que ativistas da Confederação Geral do Trabalho (CGT), uma das principais centrais sindicais francesa, se juntem ao movimento dos coletes amarelos, que organizaram protestos contra os preços dos combustíveis em 2018 e 2019.

Autoridades locais informaram que também pretendem proibir algumas manifestações em cidades como Lyon, Marselha e Montpellier.

Municípios fora da capital também foram atingidos pelos distúrbios. Em Limoges, um incêndio quase destruiu a prefeitura, um edifício do século XIX.

O primeiro-ministro francês, Sébastien Lecornu, se reuniu na última quarta-feira (21) com representantes sindicais e afirmou que uma operação de segurança de grandes proporções será organizada para sábado. O objetivo é evitar a repetição dos episódios de violência provocados por pequenos grupos, que expuseram falhas nas medidas de segurança .

Os representantes dos sindicatos disseram que a reunião não resultou em propostas concretas. Agora, as entidades concentram esforços em outra jornada de mobilização, prevista para 5 de novembro, e convocaram trabalhadores dos setores público e privado a participar.

Protestos de estudantes se transformam em movimento social

As manifestações começaram no mês passado em uma escola de ensino médio em Créteil, nos arredores de Paris, em reação à falta de funcionários. Em seguida, paralisações de aulas, bloqueios e protestos se espalharam por outros subúrbios da capital e chegaram a diferentes regiões do país, incluindo cidades menores.

Os estudantes reivindicam mais recursos para as escolas, melhorias na infraestrutura e a contratação de funcionários, principalmente em bairros de menor renda. Parte dos manifestantes também pede mudanças no sistema de ingresso nas universidades, considerado complexo e injusto por críticos.

Diante da dificuldade do governo em atender às reivindicações estudantis, os atos e bloqueios escolares passaram a incorporar outras demandas, incluindo protestos contra o aumento do custo de vida.

A ampliação do movimento ocorre meses antes da eleição presidencial de 2027, que escolherá o sucessor de Macron.

articles.title: New invention to reduce blue-green algae tested at Warminster lake
articles.summary: Experts from the University of Bath are testing out a new invention at a lake in Wiltshire.
articles.body:
Experts are testing out a new method that could see a way to tackle blue-green algae blooms.

The toxic algae is actually cyanobacteria rather than a true algae and can increase dramatically in heat, making people and animals sick when ingested.

Dr Sanjay Nagarajan, from the Institute for Sustainability and Climate Change at the University of Bath, took his child to the Warminster Pleasure Grounds in Wiltshire when he saw the lake there closed because of the bloom.

He and colleagues have since created a machine to help eliminate it from the water which he hopes he can make bigger and loan to councils.

'Shock' as new ornamental bench vandalised

From January to October this year alone there have been more than 168,000 visits to the park in Warminster.

People would usually be able to take boats out onto the lake and an active model boat club is in the area.

However, while it tends to die off in wintry weather, the algae has been causing problems over summers and this year it has been closed to activities for several months, with warning signs up round it.

"Every year it gets worse and worse with climate change," said Kevin Whitehorn, the estates manager for Warminster Town Council.

"Water levels in the lake have gone down which meant the blue-green algae has grown even more than it has done in the previous years," he added.

Nagarajan, a chemical engineer, visited the park with his child and emailed the council saying he wanted to test something.

His colleague, Dr Madhubalaji Chegu Krishnamurthi, has been studying algae for a decade and said "there many good algae as well as bad algae".

"Whenever the bad algae grows more, because of the nutrients in the lakes, it will release the various toxins that are very harmful for humans."

Nagarajan, with colleagues and a PhD student, have put together a machine with a reactor that uses bubbles to get rid of the algae. The type of reactor is not new, but its use like this is.

As with many new inventions, in order to get the water in and out of the reactor, they have had to improvise. This devices uses a generator and equipment usually used for home beer brewing.

A small box at the side does a lot of the work - Nagarajan explained that it is the reactor.

"If you take a small drinks can, fill it up with some water, heat it up and then invert it into an ice bath, it gets crushed. That's exactly what happens inside the reactor and we call it cavitation.

"Whenever we are able to manipulate the conditions to produce these cavitation bubbles, these bubbles will actually be crushed or imploding.

"Once the implosion happens those effects will help in destroying the bloom."

Nagarajan said they have had positive results: "We've seen up to 20% degradation in terms of toxins and we've also seen a lot of the algal cells being destroyed because of the effect of cavitation."

The next stage is to get their results published and apply for funding to create a bigger machine they can loan out to councils.

The claims involve alleged financial arrangements connected to Israel, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia.According to Vanity Fair, Dutch investigators gained access to a Russian military intelligence-linked server through a Russian hacker who agreed to cooperate with British and Dutch authorities. The server contained screenshots of Kushner’s iPhone, allowing investigators to view his screen as he used it.The report alleged that Kushner accessed a UAE-linked bank account that received around $750 million through transfers routed via Azerbaijan. Kushner was reportedly a signatory, although the account was not technically his.“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source familiar with the alleged arrangement told Vanity Fair.The publication alleged that UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman initially discussed funding a foreign policy fund with Kushner during Donald Trump’s first administration. It said the broader proposal did not materialise as planned, but alleged that at least $2 billion was subsequently placed in two or more accounts.“Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off,” the report said, quoting a source.Vanity Fair also alleged that around $1 billion was transferred to Israel via Azerbaijan into a separate account. articles.title: Mark Cuban sold Broadcast.com to Yahoo for $5.7 billion in 1999; years later, he launched an online business to challenge prescription drug prices
articles.summary: Mark Cuban's business career has taken him from an internet broadcasting venture that sold for billions of dollars to a pharmaceutical company built
articles.body: Mark Cuban's business career has taken him from an internet broadcasting venture that sold for billions of dollars to a pharmaceutical company built around a very different proposition. According to a Forbes report, in 1999, Yahoo acquired Broadcast.com in a deal valued at $5.7 billion, turning Cuban's early bet on online media into one of the defining transactions of the dot-com era. More than two decades later, he entered the prescription medicine market with Cost Plus Drugs, an online business intended to make the cost of medicines easier to understand and, in many cases, lower. The two ventures operate in very different industries, but both reflect Cuban's willingness to challenge established ways of doing business.How Broadcast.com turned Mark Cuban’s internet venture into a $5.7 billion Yahoo dealBroadcast.com began in 1995, when Cuban and fellow Indiana University graduate Todd Wagner set up a business to deliver audio and video over the internet. The idea developed during a period when streaming media was still unfamiliar to most households and online connections were far less capable than they are today. Cuban and Wagner saw an opportunity to distribute content to people who wanted access to broadcasts beyond the reach of conventional radio and television.Their business attracted growing attention as internet companies became increasingly valuable during the late 1990s. Yahoo, already expanding beyond its original role as a web directory, agreed to acquire Broadcast.com in 1999 in a transaction worth approximately $5.7 billion. The deal was completed largely through shares, reflecting the extraordinary valuations attached to internet businesses at the time.Broadcast.com had moved from a relatively young online venture to a company acquired for billions within four years of its founding. The transaction also placed Cuban among the entrepreneurs who benefited substantially from the expansion of internet investment before the dot-com market collapsed.Mark Cuban’s $6.8 billion fortune extends beyond his landmark internet dealCuban did not remain focused on online media after the Yahoo transaction. Over the years, his business interests extended into professional sport, entertainment and technology. His wealth has continued to reflect a range of holdings rather than a single business. Forbes' profile, updated in September 2026, lists his estimated real-time net worth at $6.8 billion as of 22 October 2026. The publication also reports that he sold a 58% stake in the Mavericks in December 2023 for an estimated $2 billion before tax, while retaining a minority interest in the team.As reported by Forbes, Cuban's route into business was not confined to technology. He has spoken about selling goods door to door as a child and taking on work, including disco lessons, to help pay for his university education. After graduating from Indiana University, he worked in the technology sector before establishing businesses of his own.His early experience with Broadcast.com remains central to his public story, but his later ventures have covered problems far removed from internet broadcasting. Cost Plus Drugs, launched in 2022, would bring him into an industry where pricing is closely tied to manufacturers, wholesalers, insurers, pharmacy benefit managers and pharmacies.How Cost Plus Drugs aims to change the way Americans pay for prescriptionsMark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company launched in January 2022 with the stated aim of making prescription medicines more affordable. Cuban co-founded the venture with physician Alex Oshmyansky, who had worked on the idea of a lower-cost pharmaceutical supply model before partnering with the entrepreneur.The company operates through an online platform that allows customers to look up medicines and purchase eligible prescriptions. Its approach places an emphasis on showing how the final price is calculated, rather than presenting the cost as a single figure with little explanation of the components behind it.Under its stated pricing model, Cost Plus Drugs adds a 15% mark-up to the cost of a medicine, alongside a pharmacy labour charge and shipping. The model was designed to offer a more transparent alternative to parts of the conventional prescription drug market, where the price paid by a patient can depend on insurance arrangements, negotiated discounts and other intermediaries.From a $5.7 billion Yahoo deal to challenging prescription drug pricesThe sale of Broadcast.com and the creation of Cost Plus Drugs sit more than 20 years apart, and the businesses have little in common at first glance. One capitalised on the growing appetite for online audio and video; the other was established around the cost and availability of prescription medicines.Yet both have involved Cuban backing a business model that offered an alternative to existing arrangements. Broadcast.com sought to make media available through the internet at a time when traditional broadcasting dominated. articles.title: Marco Rubio: Did domestic pressure make US secretary of state visit an Indian port town?
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed a business and energy agenda over diplomacy on his second trip to India this year.
articles.body:
The western Indian port town of Jamnagar is not a usual stop for foreign leaders, yet it featured prominently in US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recent visit.

So, why did Rubio visit the town? And, more importantly, why did he skip the Indian capital, Delhi?

The answer to both questions may have less to do with India and more to do with Donald Trump administration's domestic compulsions – or, more precisely, its domestic oil needs.

Rubio arrived in the financial capital Mumbai on Tuesday, where he met Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and some of the country's top business leaders. He officially ended his trip in Jamnagar - in the western state of Gujarat - home to the giant oil refinery owned by one of Asia's richest men, Mukesh Ambani.

It was his second trip to the country this year and experts say what is significant this time is the timing of the visit as well as his choice of destinations.

The Trump administration is under pressure to keep fuel prices in check ahead of November's US midterm elections, while rising tensions in the Middle East threaten global energy supplies.

With little new refining capacity expected in the immediate future in the US, India's ability to process large volumes of crude oil offers Washington a potential way to ease pressure on the fuel markets.

And that puts Reliance's Jamnagar refinery at the centre of the equation.

The visit, however, comes at a tricky moment in India-US relations. Trump has imposed tariffs on Indian goods, there are sanctions against Delhi for buying Russian energy (though currently paused) and there is a trade deal between the two countries that has remained elusive for around 20 months now.

Announcing the visit, the US State Department had earlier said that it would focus on energy cooperation, commercial investment and economic ties.

The official itinerary also did not include Delhi, which raised some questions, especially from Indian opposition politicians. But analysts say the choice was strategic.

"Delhi is where the trust gap is largest. Officials there are unhappy with a number of decisions and policies from Trump's administration," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, told the BBC.

But former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, cautions against reading too much into him skipping the capital.

"This was primarily an energy-focused visit," she says. "And after all, Rubio did meet the foreign minister in Mumbai."

The meeting between the two foreign ministers at the Taj Hotel covered trade, investment, energy security and defence cooperation, according to official statements. India's foreign ministry also said both sides welcomed progress in trade negotiations and reaffirmed their commitment to concluding a deal, which has long been in the works.

But once the diplomatic meetings were over, Rubio headed to Jamnagar, where the crown jewel of the Ambani business empire is located. This came to define the trip.

Shankar says the refinery visit "showed how much importance the US is attaching to getting more refined fuel into the market before the November midterms".

Reliance's Jamnagar complex can process about 1.4 million barrels of crude oil a day, roughly 1.5% of global refining capacity, according to the company website.

It is also a major exporter of diesel and other petroleum products, giving it a crucial role in global fuel markets.

During a tightly controlled visit on Wednesday, with limited media access, Rubio toured the facility and met members of the Ambani family, including Mukesh Ambani.

The company later released a statement, saying, "the visit included wide-ranging discussions on the global energy landscape and opportunities for commercial partnerships across conventional and new energy". It, however, did not specifically address any commitments to buy crude oil or supply refined products.

Just a day earlier, while speaking to the press, Rubio had called India a "refining superpower" and said the US wanted Reliance to process more Venezuelan oil.

"They have the capability to refine heavy crude. They've done so in the past, and I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, that's something they could do," he told reporters.

Rubio added that oil from Venezuela "can certainly provide relief" in the short term and can possibly help ease supply pressures amid tensions in the Middle East.

Reliance was once among the largest buyers of Venezuelan crude before US sanctions disrupted trade. After Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro was captured in a US intervention earlier this year and Washington eased sanctions on the country's energy sector, Reliance re-emerged as a major importer.

Experts also say the visit might ease some tensions in the Delhi-Washington relationship over India's purchase of Russian oil.

India became one of the biggest buyers of Russian oil since Moscow invaded Ukraine in 2022.

Between December 2022 and July 2026, it accounted for 37% of Russia's crude oil exports, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).

And Reliance was among the Indian companies that processed Russian crude.

In August 2025, US President Donald Trump imposed an additional 25% tariff on Indian goods over its Russian oil purchases, taking total tariffs on many Indian goods to 50%. The US, however, withdrew the additional penalty in February 2026 but India's import of Russian oil has continued to be an irritant in Washington-Delhi ties.

India has always said that securing affordable and reliable energy for its 1.4 billion people was its priority.

Then earlier this month, the US itself temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.

In that context, experts say Rubio's Jamnagar visit is aligned to three goals that the US appears to be pursuing: reducing India's dependence on Russian crude, encouraging greater imports of Venezuelan and American oil, and advancing a trade deal in which energy cooperation could become a key area of agreement.

There is also another possible business angle behind this push.

Kugelman says Rubio had two reasons to meet the Ambani family. First, to secure greater refining of Venezuelan oil and second to seek assurances that Reliance remained interested in backing a proposed Texas refinery.

In March, Trump announced a proposed refinery at the Port of Brownsville in Texas on his Truth Social platform. He said that it would be the first major new refinery in the US in 50 years.

Reliance has not publicly commented on it and there are no details on the project or when the work is expected to begin.

"The Texas facility may not be as immediately important to US interests as the arrangement tied to Venezuelan oil, but I still think it's part of the story," he says.

However, analysts point out that closer cooperation with Reliance and progress on energy security do not necessarily mean a trade deal is imminent.

"I don't think anyone really expected a trade deal to be announced at this point, but this trip seems to have helped get the relationship back on track, to the extent that it can, given the significant points of tension that remain," Kugelman said.

Rajani Sinha, the chief economist at credit rating agency CareEdge, told the BBC that greater cooperation could allay energy security concerns in both countries, help push the stalled trade negotiations forward and "boost trade and sentiment" in India.

Meera Shankar says that India is possibly "waiting for the US to formalise its tariff positions so that we know whether Delhi has a preferential trade deal".

She adds that, although ties between the two countries have been strained in recent times, their bilateral trade continues to grow.

India's merchandise exports to the US was $50.81bn between April and September, up 11.1% from the previous year, according to India's ministry of commerce. Its imports rose to $32.33bn from $25.66bn in the same period. India's merchandise trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.48bn from $20.07bn a year earlier.

"The economic relationship remains strong, but a long period of uncertainty could eventually affect it," Shankar said.

So, for now, the visit may have possibly helped get the relationship back on track, but whether that translates into a trade agreement or a lasting shift in energy ties remains to be seen.

articles.title: An Australian artist asks people to give up racist Aboriginal souvenirs, receives over 2,000 objects, including plates, tea towels and ashtrays
articles.summary: An Australian Indigenous artist has received more than 2,000 objects depicting Aboriginal people and culture after asking the public to donate racist
articles.body: An Australian Indigenous artist has received more than 2,000 objects depicting Aboriginal people and culture after asking the public to donate racist souvenirs that have circulated in homes for decades. Tony Albert launched the appeal alongside his exhibition Not a Souvenir at the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia in Sydney, inviting people to hand over items ranging from decorative crockery and tea towels to ashtrays, beer coasters and figurines. The objects, often featuring stereotypical portrayals or caricatures of Indigenous Australians, were created and sold by non-Indigenous people. Albert wants to remove them from circulation and use his artistic practice to confront the history behind their production. The response has also prompted donors to reconsider the meaning of objects they inherited, collected or once regarded as ordinary souvenirs.An artist’s appeal draws more than 2,000 donationsAlbert’s public appeal accompanied Not a Souvenir, a career-spanning exhibition that opened on May 21, 2026, at the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia in Sydney. The exhibition featured approximately 4,400 objects from his personal collection, which he began assembling as a child in the 1980s.By October 2026, members of the public had donated more than 2,000 additional items. According to The Guardian, the museum was preparing to package and ship the donations to Albert’s studio in Brisbane as the exhibition approached its closing date of October 19.The objects arrived at the museum daily, either by post or through hand-delivery. Some donations comprised dozens or hundreds of items. One included 120 plates, cups and saucers featuring Aboriginalia, while another contained 200 beer coasters. The museum also received a nearly one-metre-tall figurine depicting an Aboriginal man holding a spear.The response exceeded the expectations of the museum’s team. Assistant curator Antares Wells told The Guardian that she had initially worried the appeal might expose Albert to hateful messages. Instead, she said she had not seen any hate mail during the campaign.What is Aboriginalia and why does it matter?Aboriginalia is a term used for mass-produced souvenirs, household goods and decorative objects that depict Aboriginal people and cultures, often through stereotypes, caricatures or imagery that misrepresents Indigenous identities.These objects include ashtrays, tea towels, plates, figurines, clothing, scarves and decorative boomerangs. They became part of Australian popular and domestic culture, presenting Aboriginal people and cultural designs as commercial products.The items are significant because they reflect how Indigenous identities were represented and commodified by non-Indigenous manufacturers and sellers. Some reduced diverse Aboriginal cultures to generic images, while others portrayed Indigenous people through demeaning caricatures.Albert has collected these objects since childhood and uses them to examine the relationship between representation, colonial history and contemporary Indigenous identity. His aim is to remove such items from circulation and recontextualise them through art, encouraging people to consider the attitudes and assumptions embedded in everyday objects.Donors reconsider objects they kept for decadesThe appeal has prompted people to reflect on the history of items they inherited, bought second-hand or kept for sentimental reasons.Carolyn Ienna, a Wiradjuri artist and activist from Sydney, donated a painted image of an Aboriginal man holding a spear. They had found it in a council pickup collection more than a decade earlier.Ienna told The Guardian that looking at the object had made them feel sad, although they had not previously known the term Aboriginalia. They said the experience raised questions about the trauma of colonisation and the propaganda conveyed through representations of Aboriginal people.Lesley Pepper, who travelled from Dunedin in New Zealand to visit the exhibition, donated four porcelain plates, serviettes and placemats she had owned for around 30 to 40 years. One plate depicted a young Aboriginal woman who reminded Pepper of herself.Pepper, who has Māori heritage, said she had initially regarded the objects as a sign of respect when she acquired them from second-hand shops. She later questioned whether the woman depicted on the plate had ever been asked for permission to use her image.Another donor, Canberra resident Kathryn Hopps, handed over two silky Australian souvenir scarves inherited from her grandmother. The scarves featured kangaroos, wattle, Uluru and depictions of Aboriginal people and designs. Hopps said she had kept them because she believed they belonged in a museum, where their history could be examined.The stories accompanying these donations have become an important part of the appeal, helping to document how the objects entered people's lives and how their meaning has changed over time.A 1930s shaving mug stands out to AlbertAmong the donated objects, one that particularly struck Albert was a ceramic shaving mug from the 1930s, shaped like a caricature of an Aboriginal man's face.He told The Guardian that he found it astonishing that someone would have wanted the object in their bathroom and used it as part of an everyday routine.Albert said such objects could be rare and valuable, but their historical significance lay in what they revealed about the representation of Aboriginal people and the casual presence of these images in Australian domestic life.How Albert uses art to challenge colonial representationsAlbert’s collection is central to his artistic practice. Through sculpture, photography, painting, installation and assemblage, he reuses and reinterprets objects that were originally produced to commercialise or stereotype Aboriginal identities.His work does not simply preserve the objects as historical curiosities. It places them in a new context, encouraging audiences to question their original purpose and consider their impact.The artist has described his ambition as taking these objects out of circulation and transforming them into works that celebrate the survival and cultural vitality of Aboriginal people. The approach shifts the focus from the stereotypes imposed by the objects to the continuing presence and agency of Indigenous communities.The Not a Souvenir exhibition brings together his collection and artworks to explore the commodification and misrepresentation of Aboriginal people and cultures, while also addressing survival, resilience and cultural pride.Museum continues accepting donations after exhibitionThe Museum of Contemporary Art Australia organised the Aboriginalia appeal in partnership with Albert as part of the exhibition. Donors were also encouraged to share the history of each object and explain their relationship to it, creating a record that could accompany the physical collection.Although the museum's dedicated donation boxes were due to be removed when Not a Souvenir closed on October 19, assistant curator Antares Wells told The Guardian that the institution would continue accepting Aboriginalia and passing the objects on to Albert.The initiative has created an opportunity for members of the public to contribute to a wider examination of Australia's colonial past. Through the objects and the stories attached to them, Albert's project seeks to turn uncomfortable reminders of historical prejudice into material for education, reflection and contemporary art.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump can’t let Iran turn a military defeat into a diplomatic victory
articles.summary: Middle Eastern war history shows Tehran dragging out nuclear talks to weaken Trump before midterm elections while threatening Strait of Hormuz shipping.
articles.body: Throughout the history of Middle Eastern wars, one strategic mistake has been repeated time and again: great powers achieve victory on the battlefield, only to give their defeated adversaries an opportunity at the negotiating table to transform military defeat into political triumph. President Donald Trump faces precisely this danger. After eight months of war, the Islamic Republic of Iran, despite suffering devastating military and economic losses, continues to seek political survival through nuclear blackmail, threats to global energy security and the deliberate prolongation of negotiations. Washington must not allow a regime that has paid a heavy price for its reckless adventurism to regain, through a hastily negotiated agreement, the very position it occupied before the war. The developments of Oct. 20 demonstrate that Tehran has abandoned none of its familiar tactics of confrontation, intimidation, bluffing and extortion. On the one hand, Islamic Republic officials speak of negotiations and ending the war; on the other, they impose imaginary conditions on Washington that, if accepted without credible guarantees, could dismantle much of America's leverage. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Islamic Republic's Supreme National Security Council — a former terrorist affiliated with the Islamic terrorist group Mansouroun, who even sought to visit the United States in the 2000s but was opposed by the CIA — emphasized during his meeting with Pakistan's army chief that not a single gram of Iran's enriched uranium would leave the country. IRAN RULES OUT TRANSFERRING URANIUM TO A THIRD COUNTRY Meanwhile, Abbas Araghchi — a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps member acting as foreign minister — has made reopening the Strait of Hormuz conditional upon acceptance of Tehran's proposed plan. Far from demonstrating a genuine willingness to compromise, these positions reveal the regime's determination to preserve its instruments of coercion on the eve of a potential agreement. The most significant issue, however, lies in the political calculations of the Islamic Republic's rulers. Tehran is deliberately dragging out negotiations to weaken Trump's political standing ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections — in other words, to exert psychological pressure on the American president. IRAN REGIME UNDER PRESSURE AS REBEL GROUPS ESCALATE ATTACKS IN VOLATILE SOUTHEAST This is no longer merely a dispute over centrifuges or economic sanctions. The Islamic Republic is attempting to weaponize the exhaustion of war, the anxieties of American voters and rising energy costs as instruments of political pressure against the president of the United States. Such calculated deception must be understood in Washington as part of Tehran's asymmetric warfare strategy, not dismissed as an ordinary diplomatic tactic. The Strait of Hormuz stands at the center of this calculation. The terrorist organization known as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has claimed — without presenting any evidence — that Iranian naval mines prevented three oil tankers from passing through the waterway. Nevertheless, the widespread disruption of regional shipping is an undeniable reality. TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS The Islamic Republic understands perfectly well that it does not need to win a conventional naval battle to inflict economic pain on the United States. It need only increase the risks facing oil tankers, drive up insurance and transportation costs and keep global energy markets trapped in uncertainty. Under this strategy, commercial tankers become hostages to Tehran's security calculations, while American consumers pay the price of the Iranian regime's policies at the gas pump. This is the very essence of the rogue Islamic Republic's asymmetric warfare: a form of conflict in which military weakness is compensated for through economic, propaganda, intelligence and proxy instruments. Tehran possesses limited capabilities in a direct confrontation with American military power, but it can exploit maritime routes, militia networks, cyberattacks and influence operations to multiply the costs of the crisis. IRAN SETS RED LINES FOR US TALKS: LIFT SANCTIONS, END THREATS — 'NOT A GRAM' OF URANIUM LEAVES Reports of efforts by Iran and Russia to intensify unrest in France, together with the rearrests of two suspects in Britain on suspicion of intelligence cooperation with Iran, serve as further reminders that Western security concerns extend far beyond the Persian Gulf. Ignoring this pattern would undoubtedly be a dangerous mistake. The Islamic Republic came to power through terrorism, sustained its rule through terrorism, destruction and manufactured crises, and its eventual collapse may likewise be possible through war. The nuclear file exposes another danger. Tehran's insistence on retaining its enriched uranium, while simultaneously demanding relief from economic and military pressure, raises a fundamental question: If the Iranian regime genuinely intends to address international concerns, why does it refuse to demonstrate flexibility over one of the most sensitive components of its nuclear program? IRAN IS TRYING TO ‘CREATE A ROT FROM WITHIN’ THROUGH ‘INFORMATION WARFARE,’ ANALYST WARNS Uranium enrichment does not, by itself, prove a decision to manufacture nuclear weapons. Nevertheless, enriched uranium stockpiles, centrifuge capacity and the possibility of independent monitoring remain decisive factors in assessing the risk of a nuclear breakout. An agreement that postpones these questions while granting Tehran immediate and irreversible concessions could merely defer the crisis to an even more dangerous stage rather than resolve it. The principal global threat remains Islamic terrorism and Iran's transnational terrorist network. The Islamic Republic is attempting to weaponize the exhaustion of war, the anxieties of American voters and rising energy costs as instruments of political pressure against the president of the United States. Trump must recognize the distinction between ending military operations and eliminating a security threat. The destruction of military equipment, damage to facilities and degradation of the Revolutionary Guards' operational capabilities — however extensive — do not automatically mean the elimination of the rogue mafia regime's command structure, political will, or capacity for reconstruction. HOW SAUDI ARABIA'S DEFENSE VULNERABILITIES COULD BECOME TRUMP'S PROBLEM AMID HOUTHI ONSLAUGHT Over the decades, the Islamic Republic has demonstrated its ability to exploit periods of reduced pressure to rebuild its military and security structures and its terrorist networks. Accordingly, America's measure of success must not be limited to the cessation of missile launches or the temporary reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Genuine success will come only when the regime's ability to repeat those same threats has been curtailed. Another mistake must also be avoided: equating Iran with the Islamic Republic. The Iranian nation and the ruling establishment in Tehran are two fundamentally different realities. For years, the Iranian people have paid the price of domestic repression, systemic corruption, international isolation and the regime's regional adventurism. No sustainable American strategy should portray the survival of the Islamic Republic as synonymous with stability in Iran. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION On the contrary, a policy that merely guarantees the regime's security in exchange for temporary concessions could deprive Iranian society of the opportunity to shape a different future. While safeguarding its own national security interests, Washington must defend the Iranian people's right to determine their country's political future, without bargaining away their destiny behind the closed doors of a security agreement. The Iranian people want regime change. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP To prevent such an outcome, the Trump administration needs a clear strategic framework and a decisive course of action. Any agreement must include explicit nuclear commitments, enforceable independent monitoring, credible verification mechanisms, guarantees for maritime security and clearly defined consequences for violations. Sanctions relief and the release of financial resources must not be granted in advance without securing genuine concessions. Threats against commercial vessels must never become an instrument through which Tehran acquires political control over one of the world's most vital waterways. articles.title: Ultra-Orthodox conscription debate ignites Israel’s election battleground
articles.summary: Israel’s election heats up over ultra-Orthodox conscription debate, reflecting deep societal and political divides.
articles.body:
From the fallout of multi-fronted wars and demands for accountability over security failures to mounting concerns over the cost of living, Israelis are grappling with a series of crises ahead of the October 27 election .

Yet one contentious issue has come to dominate headlines during the campaign: whether Israel’s ultra-Orthodox Jewish minority should serve in the military.

An estimated 80,000 ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, men aged between 18 and 24 are currently avoiding military service, a figure whose significance grows with every report of staff shortages in the Israeli army.

For their political supporters in the Knesset’s Haredi Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ) parties, they are helping preserve the essential character of Israel through Torah study and prayer.

But for their detractors, they are draft dodgers refusing to undertake their share in the multiple wars Israel has embarked upon in the wake of the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023.

Critics include the self-styled Zionist opposition bloc that is locked in a tight race with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ‘s Likud Party and the far-right coalition it leads.

In May, as Haredi anger over the jailing of draft evaders spilled into street protests following a 2024 Supreme Court ruling that the military must begin drafting ultra-Orthodox men, the issue proved toxic enough to threaten Netanyahu’s government.

His ruling coalition has relied on the support of the Haredi parties in return for softening measures aimed at forcing their supporters to serve in the army. But after Netanyahu told the parties that he lacked the votes to pass an exemption bill, they pushed to dissolve the Knesset and effectively weakened the government.

On Tuesday, Netanyahu said he opposed the arrest of 40 Haredim – plural for Haredi – who were taken in for evading the draft after returning to Israel from the United States, despite a law this year meant to temporarily halt such arrests.

“We must preserve the world of Torah because it preserved us,” Netanyahu told the Haredi Kol Barama radio station. “These arrests are a deliberate attempt to harm the process of drafting Haredim without coercion.”

However, how well Netanyahu’s comments will land with the rest of the population is unclear, with the issue seen as offering an opportunity for those seeking to oust him as well as opening up divisions within his own base.

A September poll by the Israel Democracy Institute found an overwhelming 72 percent wanted to see the Haredim drafted alongside other Israelis eligible for military service.

In early October, a group of Haredim clashed with Israeli forces seeking to arrest a draft dodger in Modi’in, drawing condemnation from Netanyahu’s opponents. Former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar (“straight” or “honest”) party currently holds a narrow lead over Netanyahu’s Likud, described the incident as reflecting “the same dangerous world view that seeks to make draft evasion the norm and portray those who fulfil their duty to the state as suckers”.

He added: “That is what the upcoming election is about: Netanyahu’s draft-dodging government, or a government of conscription led by me.”

Critics of the Haredim’s refusal to serve have even found voice within Netanyahu’s party, with Likud lawmakers arguing the issue of ultra-Orthodox non-conscription could pose a threat to the future of the State of Israel.

“It is a paradox,” said Daniel Bar-Tal, a professor of psychology at Tel Aviv University.

“On the one hand, the issue of equal service unites all the secular and Zionist religious public,” he said. “On the other side, the ultra-Orthodox are rightist … This does not go together, so [Netanyahu] has a dilemma.”

Despite popular anger over the refusal to serve, and the potential consequences for their allies in the Knesset who are striving to protect that exemption, Haredi intransigence shows no sign of easing.

The two Haredi parties – Shas and UTJ – have ruled out joining any coalition that does not pass laws exempting members of their community from military service, even if it makes forming any coalition sympathetic to the ultra-Orthodox impossible.

“This is a big deal,” said Israeli pollster Mitchell Barak. “The opposition parties are trying to pitch the election as the draft dodgers versus those who protect and serve – and that is the decisive point of the election.”

Next week’s polls are the first since Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip began in October 2023, killing nearly 74,400 people and leaving most of the besieged territory in ruins, as well as the multiple conflicts across the region that followed it.

The military campaigns have placed a big burden on the state’s finances, with the high cost of living being a major source of public discontent ahead of the polls. Higher taxes have added to the economic pressure, with surveys showing that families of reservists deployed to Israel’s war zones face increased emotional and psychological strain, alongside stagnant household incomes.

According to an August survey, 42 percent of Israelis said their finances had worsened since the war on Gaza began three years ago, with the families of reservists hit hardest.

That squeeze comes as the Haredi population keeps expanding, with 1.26 million, or 12.5 percent of Israelis identified as Haredi. Projections suggest that by 2065, somewhere between 20 percent and a third of the population will be Haredi, with a large portion refusing to either work or serve in the army in place of Torah study.

“The great burden of having to serve became much more pronounced – and at the same time the Haredi sector keeps growing,” said Shmuel Rosner, a senior fellow at The Jewish People Policy Institute, “which means that a large cohort of potential soldiers does not ease the burden on others.”

He added: “The blunt refusal of Haredi leaders to even consider a change in times of such dangers demonstrated to many Israelis that this community is one that depends on Israel financially and otherwise contributes little.”
